item.title: Animal Behavior Summer Camps, 2026! — Mon Jul 27, 9:00 AM — CA
item.description:
Become an Animal Behavior Scientist for a Week! | Ages 10–15 Spend a week at Pine Trails Ranch in west Davis stepping into the role of a real animal behavior biologist! Through hands-on activities and field-style investigations, campers discover how animal behavior science protects wildlife, improves animal welfare, and opens doors to exciting careers.​ During the week, students will: Track and observe animal behavior Collect and interpret real data Explore science-based training techniques Create enrichment that keeps animals curious and thriving Study both captive and wild species
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Art Explorers: All Day Summer Arts Camp — Mon Jul 27, 9:00 AM — Davis Arts Center
item.description:
Let’s make art! Join us for a week of art adventures, friendship, and fun during Summer break. Explore ceramics, paper mache, painting, drawing, and mixed media, led by our amazing team of Teaching Artists. Camp Counselors will guide campers in fun camp activities and outdoor play. All materials are provided, just bring a water bottle, snack, sunscreen and your creativity! The week of 06/29-07/03 is broken up into individual days. Price: $550/week and $75/day
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Makerspace Drop — Mon Jul 27, 6:00 PM — YoloLab Makerspace
item.description:
Davis Makerspace is a community workspace for makers and builders, designers and inventors. A small assortment of tools will be available for use and staff or volunteers will be on hand to provide some assistance. Supervised children are welcome. Participants must provide a signed liability waiver (available on site).
Clothing Repair coaching is available on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays during Drop In Hours.
Source: Yolo Library

item.title: Intermediate Watercolor Painting with Misuk Goltz (6-Sessions) — Tue Jul 28, 10:00 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Intermediate Watercolor Painting with Misuk Goltz Tuesdays, 10 AM – 12 PM | Jun. 23, 30 & Jul. 7, 14, 21, 28 $195 Members | $215 Non-Members (Materials not included) In this 6-week course, artist Misuk Goltz will guide you through essential watercolor techniques to help you paint your favorite subjects more expressively. Sessions will cover choosing inspiring subjects and methods for creating colors, textures, and values to elevate your art. Each class includes a critique of participants’ completed work, live demonstrations, and extended individual guidance. Please note that this class is intended for participants who already have some watercolor painting experience. Register here: https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/ Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Teen Girls Summer Strength Training — Tue Jul 28, 10:30 AM — Thrive
item.description:
Want to get stronger, faster, and more confident this summer? Join our 8-Week Teen Girls Strength Training Program (Ages 13–17) 📅 June 30 – August 20 📅 Tuesdays & Thursdays at 10:30 AM ⭐ Pick Any 6 Weeks for $300 ⭐ Train All 8 Weeks for Just $350 ✔ Build muscle and confidence ✔ Learn proper lifting techniques ✔ Reduce injury risk ✔ Improve athletic performance ✔ Train in a fun, supportive environment Whether you’re preparing for your next sports season or simply want to feel stronger, this program will help you stand out from the crowd! 🔥 Stronger. Faster. More Confident. ⚠️ Space is limited and spots will fill quickly. 📧 Reserve your spot today: thrivechooseyou@gmail.com
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Elementary Educator Ceramics Workshop — Tue Jul 28, 5:30 PM — Davis Arts Center
item.description:
If you’re an elementary school teacher and have been wanting to introduce clay projects in your classroom, this three-day workshop is for you! Build your understanding of ceramics and gain the confidence to lead engaging clay projects with your students. In a supportive environment, you’ll learn kid-friendly projects that can be completed in a single day or over multiple weeks, and you’ll receive hands-on guidance in loading and firing a kiln. Connect with a creative community of fellow elementary school teachers and leave with practical skills and project ideas you can bring directly into your classroom! ● Day 1: One-day and weekly projects ● Day 2: Underglazing, textures & loading a bisque kiln ● Day 3: Glazing & loading a glaze kiln Instructor: Vex Rios (They/Them/Theirs) AGES 18+ Price: $150 Time: Tuesdays, 5:30-8:00 pm Workshop date: July 14-July 28
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Knitting & Crochet Circle — Tue Jul 28, 5:30 PM — Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch Library
item.description:

item.title: Read Forrest Featured at Performers’ Circle — Tue Jul 28, 7:00 PM — Odd Fellows Hall (Odd Fellows)
item.description:
Read Forest will sing original songs, including some new releases, and play guitar in a multi-ethnic performance of songs in English, Spanish, Portuguese and Mapudzungun. open mic from 7:00 to 8:15 pm followed by the featured performance from 8:30 to 9 pm. Rod Unema will host.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: The Artery Annual Summer Sale — Wed Jul 29 — The Artery
item.description:
Amazing Selections offered by Marvelous Artists. A Whole Month of Hot Buys. The Artery offers a cool retreat from the August sun with our Annual Summer Sale. Our artists have filled the gallery with drastically reduced treasures and will add new inventory throughout the month. Your favorite artist or one of our newest members might surprise you with a “must have” at just the right price. Our wonderful choices: Paintings, Photography, Prints, Jewelry, Woodwork, Woven baskets, Ceramics, Gourds, Greeting Cards, Fiber Art, Glass: Fused and Blown.
Source: The Dirt

item.description:
Davis location: 606 Peña Drive #300
FREE Bike Repair
Come to the Bike Garage, where our volunteer mechanics will repair your bike. We accept cash, Venmo, and Paypal donations. Interested in becoming a volunteer bike mechanic? No experience is necessary.
CONTACT US TO VOLUNTEER

item.title: Gentle yoga — Tue Aug 25, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community This is a slow and mindful practice that emphasizes deep breathing, body awareness, and nervous system regulation. This class is accessible to all abilities, providing a supportive and trauma-informed space to reconnect with the body.
Sessions alternate between floor yoga and chair yoga (on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday). Stay a bit longer on the last Tuesday of the month and join us for coffee or tea afterward!
Like all our events, this class is free, donations are welcome.
Source: Meetup: Mindful Embodied Spirituality

item.title: Davis Farmers Market - Every Saturday from 8am - 1pm — Sat Oct 10, 1:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:

Bring your family, support local growers and makers, and enjoy the bounty of our fertile region every Saturday!

item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Oct 22, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Oct 22, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Aug 12, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
